Auction of 2 Year Notes

On October 14 the Treasury announced that it would auction $4,500 million of 2 year notes to refund $1,130 million of notes maturing October 11, 1980, and to raise $1,110 million new cash. The notes offered were Treasury Notes of Series X-1982, to be dated October 11, 1980, due October 11, 1982, with interest payable on April 10 and October 11 in each year until maturity. A coupon rate of 12-1/4% was set after the determination as to which tenders were accepted on a yield basis, the average of which translated into an average accepted price close to 100.000.

Tenders for the notes were received until 1:10 p.m., EDT, October 22 and totaled $8,500 million, of which $6,500 million was accepted at yields ranging from 12.19%, price 99.888 up to 12.26%, price 99.767. Noncompetitive tenders for $1 million or less from any one bidder were accepted in full at the average yield of accepted tenders, 12.24%, price 99.801. These totaled $1,346 million. The $4,500 million of accepted tenders also included $583 million of tenders at the average price from Federal Reserve Banks as agents for foreign and international monetary authorities in exchange for securities maturing October 31, 1980.

In addition to the $4,500 million of tenders accepted in the auction process, $420 million of tenders were accepted at the average price from Government accounts and Federal Reserve Banks for their own account in exchange for maturing securities.

Tenders were received at Federal Reserve banks and branches and at the Bureau of the Public Debt, Washington, D.C., Beater notes, with interest coupons attached, and notes registered as to principal and interest were authorized to be issued in denominations of $5,000, $10,000, $100,000, and $1,000,000.

November Retunding

On October 29 the Treasury announced that it would sell to the public at auction, under competitive and noncompetitive bidding, up to $1,750 million of 11/2-year notes of Series G-1984, $2,250 million of 10-year notes of Series H-1984, and $2,000 million of 10-year bonds of 2005-10 to refund $4,922 million of publicly held Treasury securities maturing November 15, and to raise $1,100 million new cash.

A coupon rate of 11-1/4% was set on the notes of Series G 1980 after the determination as to which tenders were accepted on a yield basis, the average of which translated into an average accepted price close to 100.000. The notes of Series G-1980 will be dated November 15, 1980, due May 15, 1980, with interest payable semiannually on May 15 and November 15 until maturity.

Tenders for the notes of Series G-1986 were received until 1:10 p.m., EST, November 5, and totaled $6,451 million of which $1,752 million was accepted at yields ranging from 11.097, price 100.418, up to 11.607, price 99.592. Noncompetitive tenders for $1 million or less were accepted in full at the average yield of accepted tenders, 11.117, price 99.817. These totaled $606 million. In addition, $545 million of the notes were allotted at the average price to Federal Reserve Banks as agents for foreign and international monetary authorities in exchange for securities maturing November 15, 1980.
